chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

If a man entered Islam, acknowledged it, and then drank alcohol, committed adultery, and consumed usury, while nothing of the halal and haram had yet become clear to him, I would not carry out the legal punishment upon him if he was ignorant, unless proof were established against him that he had recited the surah in which adultery, alcohol, and consuming usury are mentioned. If he was ignorant of that, I would teach him and inform him. Then if he committed it after that, I would flog him and carry out the legal punishment upon him.

key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury or unlawful increase in financial dealings
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the faith newly entered by the person in this case
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: intoxicating drink whose consumption is forbidden

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment applied to someone who committed a forbidden act out of ignorance after entering Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that legal punishment is not applied to a newly entered Muslim who committed prohibited acts while genuinely ignorant of the relevant halal and haram. Once the ruling is conveyed and established, persistence in the act makes him liable for the prescribed hadd.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5088 - Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:

"If a man entered Islam, acknowledged it, and then drank alcohol, committed adultery, and consumed usury, without having any knowledge of what is lawful and unlawful, I would not administer the legal punishment upon him if he was ignorant - unless there was evidence that he had recited the Surah in which adultery, alcohol, and usury are mentioned. If he was unaware of that, I would inform and educate him. But if he committed those acts after that, I would flog him and enforce the legal punishment upon him."
